I'm really embarrassed about it and I have some anxiety about meeting or talking to my friends
Ive done some things like that before. I know this might sound weird but what helped me through it was to actually own it. Take control of it before they can.
Do you think it would be helpful to use humor? I don't want them to tease me about it but I don't know how else to approach it
Yea that is definitely one way to control it
Lol maybe some of my friends will share with the group too
that would definitely make me feel better about it
Ha, well that could get interesting
yes, for sure
anyway, thanks for the chat. this was helpful
Hi! How are you tonight?
I've been better. I just buried my dog yesterday
She was going to turn 15 next month
Ouch! I'm so sorry to hear that. I never lost a dog, but I've lost cats.
Is 14 a good age for a dog?
I have my first dog so I don't know much, he is 9 years old and came with our house.
Actually, yes. She was old and had dementia.
The oldest dog I evet had was 15
I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us.
How did your dog come with the house?

Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? We moved from FL to KY and the little dog just hung out here, he really belonged to the neighbor's son who didn't want him, so he just ran around wild and wouldn't leave. I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.
I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.
I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2
Thank you. that means a lot
We both had dogs when we met.
So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol

I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it!
They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes
I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.
I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.
Thanks. Another person who has pets helps
They understand

I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.

I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog.
Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.
Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed.
That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.
I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D
You too. Thanks so much. bye

I have one more thing to say - wise words from this 92 year old lady at church named Sue. She told me this after my brother died. When you get older, everyone you know is practically dead.  She said "Life is for the living, if you get caught up to much in all the death, you won't life."  True words. God bless, have a good night.
Hi Linda, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey. Honestly, it's been a tough week. Losing Max still feels so raw.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like Max meant a lot to you.
He really did. Max was more than just a pet; he was part of the family.
I can imagine it's like a part of your daily life is missing now. How are you coping?
It helps that David moved in. It's comforting not to be alone in the apartment.
That's good to hear. Having David around must provide some relief. How is the adjustment going?
It's good, but I feel guilty sometimes. Like I'm burdening him with my grief.
It's understandable to feel that way, but remember, it's okay to lean on someone you trust.
Yeah, he keeps saying he wants to be there for me, but I'm still struggling to accept help.
That can definitely be challenging. What do you think is making it hard to accept his support?
I guess I've always been independent. Relying on someone else feels foreign to me.
That makes sense. Sometimes accepting support is part of growing together. It can be a way to strengthen your bond.
You're right, and I do appreciate him being here. It's a learning process for both of us.
Absolutely. It's important to give yourself grace during this time.
I appreciate that. Talking about Max and his wagging tail makes me smile, even if it's bittersweet.
Those memories can be quite comforting. Maybe you and David can create a little tribute to Max?
That's a beautiful idea. I think it might help me honor his memory positively.
I'm glad you think so. Remember, it's okay to grieve and to find comforting ways to remember Max.
Thank you for your support. This conversation has really helped me see things from a different perspective.
You're welcome, Linda. I'm here for you anytime you need to talk.
I appreciate that a lot. I'll talk to David about your suggestion tonight.
Great. I'm sure it'll be a meaningful and healing experience for both of you.
Hi Linda, how are you holding up today?
Hey, I'm not doing too great. I had a big argument with Lily about family stuff.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be hard having a fight with someone close to you. What happened, if you feel like sharing?
We've always had different views on family responsibilities, but this time it got really heated. She thinks I'm not doing enough.
That sounds really stressful. It must be tough feeling like your efforts aren't recognized.
Yeah, exactly. I'm trying to help as much as I can, especially with work being so demanding.
Balancing work and family can be really challenging. You're doing your best, and it sounds like you're being stretched thin.
I just feel overwhelmed sometimes. I want to be there for my family but also need to take care of myself.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It's important to find a balance that works for you, too.
Then there’s the guilt. I keep thinking about how maybe I should be doing more.
Guilt can be so tough to deal with. But remember, you're only human. You're allowed to set boundaries and take care of yourself.
I know, but it's hard to shake off. I want things to be okay between Lily and me.
I understand. It shows how much you care about your relationship with her. Have you thought about how you might approach things with Lily moving forward?
I've been thinking of reaching out and talking it over calmly. I don't want this to become a bigger issue.
That sounds like a really thoughtful approach. Clear communication might help both of you understand each other better.
I hope so. I just hate being in this kind of conflict. It feels exhausting.
Conflicts can be really draining, but resolving them can also lead to stronger bonds. You're strong for facing it head-on.
Thanks for saying that. I guess I'll try to focus on the good side of it.
Absolutely. Lean on David too; he's there to support you. How are things going with him?
He's been great, actually. Moving in together has been a big help for me emotionally, especially after losing my dog.
It's wonderful to hear you have that support. David seems like a solid rock for you during tough times.
Yeah, he's been amazing. I think I'll talk to him more about how I'm feeling too.
That's a good idea. Keeping him in the loop can only strengthen your relationship.
I'll definitely do that. Thanks for listening to me today, it really helps to talk things out.
Anytime, Linda. I'm here whenever you need to chat. You're doing great, just take it one step at a time.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now. Mind lending an ear?
Of course, Linda. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I just adopted a new puppy, and while I thought it would help, I’m feeling all sorts of things I didn’t expect.
Adopting a new puppy sounds like a big step. What feelings are coming up for you?
I thought it would ease the pain of losing Max. But sometimes, it feels like I'm trying to replace him.
Losing Max was really tough on you. It's understandable to have mixed emotions. It's okay to miss him while also making room for new love.
Thank you for saying that. I just feel guilty, like I'm betraying Max's memory by loving another dog.
Guilt is a common feeling, but remember, Max would want you to be happy and give love to another dog. You're not replacing him; you're honoring the love you shared by opening your heart again.
I know, logically, you’re right. I guess it's just my heart struggling to catch up.
That's completely normal, Linda. Healing takes time, and you're doing your best. How is the new puppy helping, if at all?
Well, he’s full of energy and brings some chaos into my routine, which is a nice distraction. But sometimes, I feel overwhelmed trying to train him.
It sounds like he's bringing some lively energy into your life, but it's okay to feel overwhelmed. It's a big adjustment for both of you.
Exactly. And with David moving in, I worry about how all these changes are affecting us.
That's a lot to juggle. How's your relationship with David? Is he supportive with all these changes?
David's been wonderful. Having him here helps, but I fear I'm relying on him too much.
It's great that David is there for support. It's okay to lean on him during tough times, as long as you communicate and find balance together.
I'll keep that in mind. I just need to find my own footing amidst everything that's happening.
You will. You're taking steps by adopting a new puppy and being honest about your feelings. It shows strength and courage.
Thanks for saying that. It's just been a whirlwind lately, and I appreciate having someone to talk it through with.
Anytime, Linda. Remember, it's okay to feel however you feel right now. You're doing an amazing job taking care of yourself and embracing change.
Hi Linda, how are you feeling today?
Hey, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed at the moment.
I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to share what's been going on?
It's been a lot at work. The pressure has really been getting to me lately, and I actually had a panic attack a few days ago.
That sounds really tough. Panic attacks can be so frightening. Have you been able to talk to anyone about it?
I mentioned it to David. He's been there for me, but sometimes I feel like it's unfair to burden him with my issues.
It's great that David is supportive, but remember, your feelings and experiences are valid, and it's okay to lean on him during tough times.
Thank you. I just wish I could manage my stress better. I thought adopting Buddy would help, but I still find myself feeling anxious.
Pets can be comforting, but it's understandable to still feel anxious, especially with work pressures piling up. Have you had a chance to take any breaks or do something relaxing lately?
Not really. The deadlines are so tight, and I'm constantly worried about falling behind.
I can imagine that makes it hard to decompress. Perhaps finding small moments in the day for yourself could help, even if it's just a few minutes.
That might be worth trying. Maybe a short walk with Buddy could help clear my head.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Buddy would probably love that too!
Yeah, he probably would. I also think I need to re-evaluate how I'm handling work stress. This panic attack was a wake-up call.
It's impressive that you're reflecting on this and considering changes. Recognizing the need for balance is such a big step.
Thank you. I really appreciate the encouragement. I also need to find a way to mend things with Lily. Our argument has been weighing on me too.
Family dynamics can be challenging, especially after a disagreement. It's understandable you're feeling down about it.
Yeah, I hope I can find a way to apologize and move forward. I've been hesitant to reach out.
Taking the first step can be daunting, but it could lead to healing for both of you. Maybe just starting with a message to say you miss her could open the door.
That's a good idea. I'll try to write her something sincere. I really hope we can patch things up.
Your willingness to reconcile shows just how much you value your relationship with her. I'm hopeful for you both.
Thanks. It means a lot to have someone to talk to about all this. I'm feeling a bit more hopeful now.
I'm glad to hear that, Linda. Remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk. You've got this!
Hey Linda! How have you been holding up since deciding to take some time off work?
Hi. It's been a mix of emotions honestly. It feels strange not to be in the office, but I know I need this break.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Taking a pause can sometimes feel unsettling, but it's important to prioritize your wellbeing. How are you coping with everything so far?
I've had some good days and some not-so-good days. I've been trying to make the most of my time, but it's hard not to worry about falling behind at work.
It’s only natural to feel anxious about work. Remember, you've made this decision for a reason. It's okay to focus on your health right now.
You're right. I just hope I won't let my team down. I had a panic attack last month, and it really shook me.
I'm so sorry to hear that, Linda. Panic attacks can be incredibly overwhelming. Have you had any more incidents since then?
Thankfully, no more since then. But it’s been hard to shake the fear off. David’s been really supportive though, and Buddy has been a great distraction.

It's wonderful to hear that David and Buddy have been comforting. Having supportive loved ones around can make such a difference. Have they been helping you with any specific strategies or just being there when you need them?
David's been encouraging me to talk things out and we've been going for walks with Buddy, which helps me clear my mind. I guess it's the little things, you know?
Absolutely, those little moments can be quite powerful. Is there anything else you've found helpful during this time to manage your stress?
I've started journaling a bit. I think putting my thoughts on paper helps me process them better. Plus, it helps distract me from worrying about work.
That sounds like a great way to process emotions. Writing can be so cathartic. Have you been able to reach any new insights about your situation through journaling?
I guess I've realized that I need to set clearer boundaries. I tend to take on too much, and it eventually gets overwhelming.

That’s a very important realization, Linda. Setting boundaries can be challenging, but it’s crucial for your mental health. Have you thought about any specific steps you can take to start creating those boundaries when you return to work?
I’m considering having a talk with my manager about my workload. Mike has been understanding in the past, and I'm hopeful he'll support a more manageable schedule.

It sounds like a rational plan and I’m glad you’re thinking of discussing this with Mike. Remember, advocating for yourself is key. How have things been with Lily lately? Any better since your last conversation?
We’ve had a couple of talks since the argument. It’s still a bit tense, but I think we’re starting to understand each other more. It’ll take time, but I’m hopeful.
That’s a good start, and it’s great that you’re both taking steps towards reconciliation. It’s important to be patient with each other. Anything else on your mind that you'd like to share?
Not at the moment. Just trying to take things one day at a time. Thanks for listening, it really helps to talk about these things.
Anytime, Linda. Remember that you have support and are doing your best. Feel free to reach out whenever you need someone to talk to. Take care of yourself!
Hey, I hope you don't mind me reaching out again. I just have a lot on my mind lately.
Of course, Linda! I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, David proposed recently, and it's been a whirlwind of emotions since then. It's exciting but also a bit overwhelming.
That sounds like a big moment! It makes sense that you'd be feeling a mix of excitement and pressure.
Exactly, I mean I love him, but I can't help thinking about all the decisions that follow. There's just so much to consider.
It sounds like you're putting a lot of pressure on yourself. It's okay to take things one step at a time.
Yeah, you're right. I guess it's also because of everything else that's been happening. Like, I took a leave from work and I'm trying to figure things out.
Taking a leave was a big step, Linda. It's important to focus on your mental well-being, especially with so much happening.
And then there's my sister, Lily. We've had some tension over family responsibilities, and it just feels like everything's piling up.
I remember you mentioned that argument with Lily. Have you had a chance to talk things out with her since then?
Not really. Every time I think about bringing it up, I just get anxious. I don’t know how to start without things getting heated again.
Conversations like that can be tough, but maybe focusing on how you're feeling could help steer it in a different direction.
True. I guess expressing my feelings without accusations could make a difference. I should probably give it more thought.
That's a great approach, Linda. It takes courage to try, and it might just bring the clarity you're looking for.
I hope so. On a lighter note, Buddy is growing up so fast, and he’s been a real joy to have around.
Oh, that sounds wonderful! Puppies can bring so much happiness and comfort, especially during challenging times.
Definitely. He’s been a great distraction, and taking care of him helps me clear my mind a bit.
It's amazing how pets can be such good therapy, isn't it? Make sure to cherish those moments with Buddy.
I will, for sure. Thanks for listening, it really means a lot to have someone to talk this all through.
Anytime, Linda. I believe you're stronger than you realize, and you're making great progress in navigating everything.
I appreciate that reminder. I’ll try to take things day by day and see where it all goes.
That sounds like a solid plan. And always remember, you're not alone in this journey.
Hey Linda, how have you been feeling lately? I heard some good news about you and Lily reconnecting.
Hi, yeah, Lily reached out and apologized. It's been nice, but it brought up a lot of feelings.
I can imagine. How do you feel about the apology and reconnecting with her?
Relieved in some ways. I missed having her around and it's a weight off my shoulders. But it's also made me think about all the things we have yet to address.
That's understandable. Repairing relationships can be a complex process. Did you get a chance to talk about those unresolved issues?
Not yet really. We touched on the argument a little bit, but I think we're both cautious about dredging up old stuff too quickly.
That makes sense. Taking things slow can be really important to make sure both of you feel comfortable.
Yes, exactly. And part of me wonders if we're just pretending everything is fine instead of really working through it.
It's normal to have those worries after a conflict. Perhaps setting some time to discuss things openly might help?
I've thought about that. Maybe initiating a more open dialogue could help, but I'm anxious about how to bring it up without causing another argument.
Approaching it with openness and empathy might ease tensions. Remember the progress you've already made and the shared desire for a better relationship.
True. Having David around has really helped me find the courage to face some of these issues, too.
David seems to be a great support for you. Has his presence also influenced how you see your relationship with Lily?
Definitely. Watching how supportive he is and how we handle things together gives me hope that Lily and I can do the same.
It's beautiful to hear that. With empathy and patience, you can build a stronger connection with her.
I really hope so. It's comforting to know we're on better terms heading into my wedding planning.
Absolutely, it sounds like a positive step forward. How are you feeling about the wedding planning amidst everything?
Excited but also a bit overwhelmed. There’s so much to do, but having my sister there now feels reassuring.
It's a lot, but try to take it one step at a time. With loved ones by your side, especially Lily and David, it can also be a joyful experience.
Thanks, I needed to hear that. Focusing on the positive aspects really makes a difference.
I'm glad I could help. You’re doing great, Linda. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Hey, I just got back from the doctor.
Hi Linda. How did it go? Are you okay?
The doctor said my stress levels are through the roof. It was a bit of a wake-up call, honestly.
That sounds really concerning. I'm glad you went to see a doctor. What did they suggest?
They told me I need to find ways to manage my stress better. But with everything going on, it just feels overwhelming.
I can only imagine how much you're juggling right now. It makes sense that it's a lot to handle. Have you thought about any specific steps you might take?
I've been thinking about trying meditation, and maybe pick up some light exercise routines. But it's hard with the wedding planning and work stuff.
Those sound like great ideas. It's tough, but it might help you find some peace amidst the chaos. How's the wedding planning going, by the way?
It's exciting but also stressful. There's so much to organize and David and I are still figuring out some of the details.
It's understandable to feel that way. It's a big step, but also a joyous one. How have you and David been handling the pressure together?
David's been really supportive, especially after these health issues came up. He's been reminding me it's okay to slow down and take care of myself.
That's wonderful to hear. Having someone like David must be comforting. Have you thought about leaning on any of your other support systems?
I've reconnected with my sister Lily. She's been really understanding about everything that's happened in the past. We even laughed about our old arguments recently.
That's so heartening to hear, Linda. Family can be a great source of strength. How's it been with Buddy, your puppy?
Buddy is a little ball of energy. He makes me smile every day, which is helping a lot.
That's so lovely. Dogs can bring so much joy and relieve stress. It's good to hear you have a little bit of joy and laughter with him.
Yeah, it feels nice to have that balance, even just for moments. I'm just worried I won't keep up with everything and it'll affect my health again.
It's completely normal to feel that worry, Linda. It's tough, but take each day as it comes. Remember to prioritize your health, and lean on your support systems.
Thank you. I really appreciate these talks. It's like a breath of fresh air during all this chaos.
I'm always here to listen, Linda. You're doing an amazing job handling everything. Just take it one step at a time and remember you're not alone in this.
Hey, thanks for being here. I just need to talk a bit.
Of course, Linda. What's on your mind?
I've been trying to keep up with everything, but it's just a lot. Work, wedding plans, and now I've added meditation into the mix to help with stress.
It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. How is the meditation going so far?
It's been interesting. Some days it helps, and other days it's hard to focus. I keep thinking about the next thing I need to do.
That's understandable. It's hard to quiet the mind when so much is happening. Have you noticed any particular moments when stress hits the hardest?
Usually when I'm at home trying to relax, ironically. David is supportive, but I feel guilty about how much I'm depending on him.
Leaning on someone you love isn't a bad thing, Linda. Have you talked to David about how you're feeling?
Not in depth. I think I'm scared he'll think I'm not ready for the commitment if I show too much of my stress.
It's important to let him in on your struggles. He might surprise you with how understanding he is. Plus, it might ease some of your stress sharing it with him.
You're right. I suppose I've always been the type to handle things on my own, even when I was arguing with Lily. But, it's exhausting.
You've come a long way since then, reestablishing your bond with Lily and even adopting Buddy for emotional support. It's okay to embrace new support systems.
Buddy has been a joy, definitely helps lift my spirits on rough days. I forgot how much a pet can change the atmosphere.
Pets have a special way of comforting us. It's like they know when we need a little extra love. How's Buddy adjusting?
He's a bundle of energy and keeps me distracted in a good way. Sometimes, I wish I could have his carefree attitude.
Sounds like Buddy is a wonderful addition. And taking things one moment at a time, like he does, might help. How has your health been since the doctor's visit?
The meditation is helping, slowly. My doctor suggested regular breaks from wedding planning and work emails to keep things in balance.
That sounds like solid advice. Creating boundaries can be really beneficial. Would David be able to help with some of the planning?
I think he would. I've been hesitant to delegate, but maybe it's time to ease my load a bit.
Letting go of some of the responsibilities can relieve a lot of pressure. You're already doing so much just by working on your mental health.
Thank you. I guess I needed a reminder that it's okay to ask for help and not do everything alone.
Exactly. You're doing your best and that's all anyone can ask. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Thanks for talking this through with me. I feel a little lighter knowing I have support.
Anytime, Linda. Just keep breathing and reaching out whenever you need someone to listen.
Hey Linda, how have you been holding up lately?
Not too great, to be honest. Things are really tense between David and me right now.
I’m sorry to hear that. Is it about the wedding plans?
Yeah, we had our first big argument about it. It feels overwhelming.
Conflicts about wedding planning can be quite stressful. What specifically was the disagreement about?
David and I have different visions for the wedding, and it's hard to find a middle ground.
That sounds really challenging. Have you been able to talk it out since the argument?
We tried talking about it, but it's like we're speaking different languages on this topic.
It's tough to be on different pages with someone you care about. How are you feeling about the whole situation?
Honestly, I'm feeling anxious and it's triggering some of my previous stress issues.
Given your past experiences with stress, that must be really hard to navigate. Have you been keeping up with meditation or any other techniques to manage your anxiety?
I've been trying to meditate when I can, but it's difficult with everything else going on.
It's understandable that it might be difficult to focus right now. Maybe a small step could help, like setting aside just a few minutes each day?
That's a good idea, maybe I can try short sessions in the morning.
That sounds like a positive step. How's your relationship with your sister Lily going? I remember you two had reconnected recently.
It's been better. Lily's been supportive, which is nice, especially with everything going on right now.
It's great that you have her support. Maybe she could be someone to talk to about the wedding planning stresses too?
Yeah, I think it might help. She did offer to help once before all this started.
It might provide some relief to have a trusted family member involved. How about Buddy? How's your new puppy doing in all of this?
Buddy's been a little ball of sunshine. Having him around has been comforting.
Sometimes our pets give us just what we need, without even knowing it.
Definitely. It's nice to focus on his happiness even when things feel chaotic.
That’s wonderful. Remember, you’re not alone in this—between Buddy, Lily, and me, you have a great support system.
Thank you. It really helps knowing I can talk to you and lean on others.
Any time, Linda. I’m here whenever you need to talk or figure things out. Take it one step at a time.

current_prefix.text: Hi Linda, how have you been doing lately?
Hey, I've been having a tough time recently. I've started having recurring dreams about my late dog.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like it must be hard for you. How do these dreams make you feel?
It's bittersweet. In the dreams, I'm always so happy to see him, but when I wake up, the loss hits all over again.
That makes a lot of sense. Grief can be so tricky and overwhelming. Do you remember specific moments in the dreams that stand out?
Yes, it's always us playing in the park or snuggling on the couch. They were such ordinary moments but meant the world to me.
Those memories hold a lot of meaning. It's understandable they manifest in your dreams. Do you think there might be something triggering this pattern?
I wonder if it's because I've been feeling stressed with the wedding planning and work. Maybe Max symbolized comfort for me.

turns.text: HI there, how are you doing?
Hi, I'm ok
Do you want to talk about whats going on right now?
Sure. I took a nude photo of myself to share with someone I'm dating, and accidentally sent it to several friends in a group chat
I'm really embarrassed about it and I have some anxiety about meeting or talking to my friends
Ive done some things like that before. I know this might sound weird but what helped me through it was to actually own it. Take control of it before they can.
Do you think it would be helpful to use humor? I don't want them to tease me about it but I don't know how else to approach it
Yea that is definitely one way to control it
Lol maybe some of my friends will share with the group too
that would definitely make me feel better about it
Ha, well that could get interesting
yes, for sure
anyway, thanks for the chat. this was helpful
Hi! How are you tonight?
I've been better. I just buried my dog yesterday
She was going to turn 15 next month
Ouch! I'm so sorry to hear that. I never lost a dog, but I've lost cats.
Is 14 a good age for a dog?
I have my first dog so I don't know much, he is 9 years old and came with our house.
Actually, yes. She was old and had dementia.
The oldest dog I evet had was 15
I'm so sorry, losing a pet is very hard on us.
How did your dog come with the house?

Was that your only pet? Or do you have others? We moved from FL to KY and the little dog just hung out here, he really belonged to the neighbor's son who didn't want him, so he just ran around wild and wouldn't leave. I never had a dog, but it got cold, so i took him in. They never asked about him and after a week, I asked them if I could have the dog, so they said yes. I don't think they cared.
I wish I could give you a hug, really, there are no words to make this better as you already know the grief of losing a pet, it does get better, but it stings terribly at first.
I have 2 other dogs that are mine and my boyfriend has 2
Thank you. that means a lot
We both had dogs when we met.
So you definitely are a dog lover! I was in my 50s before I ever had a dog, now I wish I had more, they are really loving. Not like cats who don't care much about much except FOOD! lol

I know when tragedy happens, I can't get stuck in depression, I sort of have to force myself to put one foot in front of the other. It's hard to have a healthy balance between grieving and continuing to live. Cry, then dry my eyes, pick up, go for a walk, don't get caught in grief, but yet don't deny it!
They get to be so close and you can really pick up on their emotions and stuff. That's what happens to me. I get stuck sometimes
I get stuck too. But you are doing the right things, here you reached out to someone and I do care, so you are moving forward.
I always find it helpful just so have someone share my pain with me. Just to know I'm  not alone.
Thanks. Another person who has pets helps
They understand

I do understand. My mom died in 2010, right after she died, 1 of my cats died, my husband went into the hospital and almost died, so we went on vacation so I would not be consumed with grief, and do you know, we brought our pets and our cat died when we arrived here on vacation?  I will never forget that. You know what. I knew I could either get consumed in grief, or push through. Man, that was hard. I prayed a lot and God got me through that and I had a good vacation, all things considered.

I will definitely pray for you too that God will comfort your heart and that you will be comforted by your other dogs and your boyfriend's dogs and that you will feel joy at times at the happy memories you had with your dog.
Oh wow, that sounds horrible. Pushing through though I guess is all one can do then. Thank you so much. I believe in prayer.
Prayer is what gets me through every day!  :D  It was rough, but I believe these hard times strengthen us in some way. Because life throws hard balls, and we have to move forward or be consumed.
That's true. I'm glad I did this project. You really helped me.
I'm so glad I did too. It was a pleasure to meet you. And once again, (hug). :D
You too. Thanks so much. bye

I have one more thing to say - wise words from this 92 year old lady at church named Sue. She told me this after my brother died. When you get older, everyone you know is practically dead.  She said "Life is for the living, if you get caught up to much in all the death, you won't life."  True words. God bless, have a good night.
Hi Linda, how have you been feeling lately?
Hey. Honestly, it's been a tough week. Losing Max still feels so raw.
I'm really sorry to hear that. It sounds like Max meant a lot to you.
He really did. Max was more than just a pet; he was part of the family.
I can imagine it's like a part of your daily life is missing now. How are you coping?
It helps that David moved in. It's comforting not to be alone in the apartment.
That's good to hear. Having David around must provide some relief. How is the adjustment going?
It's good, but I feel guilty sometimes. Like I'm burdening him with my grief.
It's understandable to feel that way, but remember, it's okay to lean on someone you trust.
Yeah, he keeps saying he wants to be there for me, but I'm still struggling to accept help.
That can definitely be challenging. What do you think is making it hard to accept his support?
I guess I've always been independent. Relying on someone else feels foreign to me.
That makes sense. Sometimes accepting support is part of growing together. It can be a way to strengthen your bond.
You're right, and I do appreciate him being here. It's a learning process for both of us.
Absolutely. It's important to give yourself grace during this time.
I appreciate that. Talking about Max and his wagging tail makes me smile, even if it's bittersweet.
Those memories can be quite comforting. Maybe you and David can create a little tribute to Max?
That's a beautiful idea. I think it might help me honor his memory positively.
I'm glad you think so. Remember, it's okay to grieve and to find comforting ways to remember Max.
Thank you for your support. This conversation has really helped me see things from a different perspective.
You're welcome, Linda. I'm here for you anytime you need to talk.
I appreciate that a lot. I'll talk to David about your suggestion tonight.
Great. I'm sure it'll be a meaningful and healing experience for both of you.
Hi Linda, how are you holding up today?
Hey, I'm not doing too great. I had a big argument with Lily about family stuff.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must be hard having a fight with someone close to you. What happened, if you feel like sharing?
We've always had different views on family responsibilities, but this time it got really heated. She thinks I'm not doing enough.
That sounds really stressful. It must be tough feeling like your efforts aren't recognized.
Yeah, exactly. I'm trying to help as much as I can, especially with work being so demanding.
Balancing work and family can be really challenging. You're doing your best, and it sounds like you're being stretched thin.
I just feel overwhelmed sometimes. I want to be there for my family but also need to take care of myself.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. It's important to find a balance that works for you, too.
Then there’s the guilt. I keep thinking about how maybe I should be doing more.
Guilt can be so tough to deal with. But remember, you're only human. You're allowed to set boundaries and take care of yourself.
I know, but it's hard to shake off. I want things to be okay between Lily and me.
I understand. It shows how much you care about your relationship with her. Have you thought about how you might approach things with Lily moving forward?
I've been thinking of reaching out and talking it over calmly. I don't want this to become a bigger issue.
That sounds like a really thoughtful approach. Clear communication might help both of you understand each other better.
I hope so. I just hate being in this kind of conflict. It feels exhausting.
Conflicts can be really draining, but resolving them can also lead to stronger bonds. You're strong for facing it head-on.
Thanks for saying that. I guess I'll try to focus on the good side of it.
Absolutely. Lean on David too; he's there to support you. How are things going with him?
He's been great, actually. Moving in together has been a big help for me emotionally, especially after losing my dog.
It's wonderful to hear you have that support. David seems like a solid rock for you during tough times.
Yeah, he's been amazing. I think I'll talk to him more about how I'm feeling too.
That's a good idea. Keeping him in the loop can only strengthen your relationship.
I'll definitely do that. Thanks for listening to me today, it really helps to talk things out.
Anytime, Linda. I'm here whenever you need to chat. You're doing great, just take it one step at a time.
Hey, I could really use someone to talk to right now. Mind lending an ear?
Of course, Linda. I'm here for you. What's on your mind?
I just adopted a new puppy, and while I thought it would help, I’m feeling all sorts of things I didn’t expect.
Adopting a new puppy sounds like a big step. What feelings are coming up for you?
I thought it would ease the pain of losing Max. But sometimes, it feels like I'm trying to replace him.
Losing Max was really tough on you. It's understandable to have mixed emotions. It's okay to miss him while also making room for new love.
Thank you for saying that. I just feel guilty, like I'm betraying Max's memory by loving another dog.
Guilt is a common feeling, but remember, Max would want you to be happy and give love to another dog. You're not replacing him; you're honoring the love you shared by opening your heart again.
I know, logically, you’re right. I guess it's just my heart struggling to catch up.
That's completely normal, Linda. Healing takes time, and you're doing your best. How is the new puppy helping, if at all?
Well, he’s full of energy and brings some chaos into my routine, which is a nice distraction. But sometimes, I feel overwhelmed trying to train him.
It sounds like he's bringing some lively energy into your life, but it's okay to feel overwhelmed. It's a big adjustment for both of you.
Exactly. And with David moving in, I worry about how all these changes are affecting us.
That's a lot to juggle. How's your relationship with David? Is he supportive with all these changes?
David's been wonderful. Having him here helps, but I fear I'm relying on him too much.
It's great that David is there for support. It's okay to lean on him during tough times, as long as you communicate and find balance together.
I'll keep that in mind. I just need to find my own footing amidst everything that's happening.
You will. You're taking steps by adopting a new puppy and being honest about your feelings. It shows strength and courage.
Thanks for saying that. It's just been a whirlwind lately, and I appreciate having someone to talk it through with.
Anytime, Linda. Remember, it's okay to feel however you feel right now. You're doing an amazing job taking care of yourself and embracing change.
Hi Linda, how are you feeling today?
Hey, I'm feeling pretty overwhelmed at the moment.
I'm sorry to hear that. Would you like to share what's been going on?
It's been a lot at work. The pressure has really been getting to me lately, and I actually had a panic attack a few days ago.
That sounds really tough. Panic attacks can be so frightening. Have you been able to talk to anyone about it?
I mentioned it to David. He's been there for me, but sometimes I feel like it's unfair to burden him with my issues.
It's great that David is supportive, but remember, your feelings and experiences are valid, and it's okay to lean on him during tough times.
Thank you. I just wish I could manage my stress better. I thought adopting Buddy would help, but I still find myself feeling anxious.
Pets can be comforting, but it's understandable to still feel anxious, especially with work pressures piling up. Have you had a chance to take any breaks or do something relaxing lately?
Not really. The deadlines are so tight, and I'm constantly worried about falling behind.
I can imagine that makes it hard to decompress. Perhaps finding small moments in the day for yourself could help, even if it's just a few minutes.
That might be worth trying. Maybe a short walk with Buddy could help clear my head.
That sounds like a wonderful idea. Buddy would probably love that too!
Yeah, he probably would. I also think I need to re-evaluate how I'm handling work stress. This panic attack was a wake-up call.
It's impressive that you're reflecting on this and considering changes. Recognizing the need for balance is such a big step.
Thank you. I really appreciate the encouragement. I also need to find a way to mend things with Lily. Our argument has been weighing on me too.
Family dynamics can be challenging, especially after a disagreement. It's understandable you're feeling down about it.
Yeah, I hope I can find a way to apologize and move forward. I've been hesitant to reach out.
Taking the first step can be daunting, but it could lead to healing for both of you. Maybe just starting with a message to say you miss her could open the door.
That's a good idea. I'll try to write her something sincere. I really hope we can patch things up.
Your willingness to reconcile shows just how much you value your relationship with her. I'm hopeful for you both.
Thanks. It means a lot to have someone to talk to about all this. I'm feeling a bit more hopeful now.
I'm glad to hear that, Linda. Remember, I'm here whenever you need to talk. You've got this!
Hey Linda! How have you been holding up since deciding to take some time off work?
Hi. It's been a mix of emotions honestly. It feels strange not to be in the office, but I know I need this break.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Taking a pause can sometimes feel unsettling, but it's important to prioritize your wellbeing. How are you coping with everything so far?
I've had some good days and some not-so-good days. I've been trying to make the most of my time, but it's hard not to worry about falling behind at work.
It’s only natural to feel anxious about work. Remember, you've made this decision for a reason. It's okay to focus on your health right now.
You're right. I just hope I won't let my team down. I had a panic attack last month, and it really shook me.
I'm so sorry to hear that, Linda. Panic attacks can be incredibly overwhelming. Have you had any more incidents since then?
Thankfully, no more since then. But it’s been hard to shake the fear off. David’s been really supportive though, and Buddy has been a great distraction.

It's wonderful to hear that David and Buddy have been comforting. Having supportive loved ones around can make such a difference. Have they been helping you with any specific strategies or just being there when you need them?
David's been encouraging me to talk things out and we've been going for walks with Buddy, which helps me clear my mind. I guess it's the little things, you know?
Absolutely, those little moments can be quite powerful. Is there anything else you've found helpful during this time to manage your stress?
I've started journaling a bit. I think putting my thoughts on paper helps me process them better. Plus, it helps distract me from worrying about work.
That sounds like a great way to process emotions. Writing can be so cathartic. Have you been able to reach any new insights about your situation through journaling?
I guess I've realized that I need to set clearer boundaries. I tend to take on too much, and it eventually gets overwhelming.

That’s a very important realization, Linda. Setting boundaries can be challenging, but it’s crucial for your mental health. Have you thought about any specific steps you can take to start creating those boundaries when you return to work?
I’m considering having a talk with my manager about my workload. Mike has been understanding in the past, and I'm hopeful he'll support a more manageable schedule.

It sounds like a rational plan and I’m glad you’re thinking of discussing this with Mike. Remember, advocating for yourself is key. How have things been with Lily lately? Any better since your last conversation?
We’ve had a couple of talks since the argument. It’s still a bit tense, but I think we’re starting to understand each other more. It’ll take time, but I’m hopeful.
That’s a good start, and it’s great that you’re both taking steps towards reconciliation. It’s important to be patient with each other. Anything else on your mind that you'd like to share?
Not at the moment. Just trying to take things one day at a time. Thanks for listening, it really helps to talk about these things.
Anytime, Linda. Remember that you have support and are doing your best. Feel free to reach out whenever you need someone to talk to. Take care of yourself!
Hey, I hope you don't mind me reaching out again. I just have a lot on my mind lately.
Of course, Linda! I'm here for you. What's been going on?
Well, David proposed recently, and it's been a whirlwind of emotions since then. It's exciting but also a bit overwhelming.
That sounds like a big moment! It makes sense that you'd be feeling a mix of excitement and pressure.
Exactly, I mean I love him, but I can't help thinking about all the decisions that follow. There's just so much to consider.
It sounds like you're putting a lot of pressure on yourself. It's okay to take things one step at a time.
Yeah, you're right. I guess it's also because of everything else that's been happening. Like, I took a leave from work and I'm trying to figure things out.
Taking a leave was a big step, Linda. It's important to focus on your mental well-being, especially with so much happening.
And then there's my sister, Lily. We've had some tension over family responsibilities, and it just feels like everything's piling up.
I remember you mentioned that argument with Lily. Have you had a chance to talk things out with her since then?
Not really. Every time I think about bringing it up, I just get anxious. I don’t know how to start without things getting heated again.
Conversations like that can be tough, but maybe focusing on how you're feeling could help steer it in a different direction.
True. I guess expressing my feelings without accusations could make a difference. I should probably give it more thought.
That's a great approach, Linda. It takes courage to try, and it might just bring the clarity you're looking for.
I hope so. On a lighter note, Buddy is growing up so fast, and he’s been a real joy to have around.
Oh, that sounds wonderful! Puppies can bring so much happiness and comfort, especially during challenging times.
Definitely. He’s been a great distraction, and taking care of him helps me clear my mind a bit.
It's amazing how pets can be such good therapy, isn't it? Make sure to cherish those moments with Buddy.
I will, for sure. Thanks for listening, it really means a lot to have someone to talk this all through.
Anytime, Linda. I believe you're stronger than you realize, and you're making great progress in navigating everything.
I appreciate that reminder. I’ll try to take things day by day and see where it all goes.
That sounds like a solid plan. And always remember, you're not alone in this journey.
Hey Linda, how have you been feeling lately? I heard some good news about you and Lily reconnecting.
Hi, yeah, Lily reached out and apologized. It's been nice, but it brought up a lot of feelings.
I can imagine. How do you feel about the apology and reconnecting with her?
Relieved in some ways. I missed having her around and it's a weight off my shoulders. But it's also made me think about all the things we have yet to address.
That's understandable. Repairing relationships can be a complex process. Did you get a chance to talk about those unresolved issues?
Not yet really. We touched on the argument a little bit, but I think we're both cautious about dredging up old stuff too quickly.
That makes sense. Taking things slow can be really important to make sure both of you feel comfortable.
Yes, exactly. And part of me wonders if we're just pretending everything is fine instead of really working through it.
It's normal to have those worries after a conflict. Perhaps setting some time to discuss things openly might help?
I've thought about that. Maybe initiating a more open dialogue could help, but I'm anxious about how to bring it up without causing another argument.
Approaching it with openness and empathy might ease tensions. Remember the progress you've already made and the shared desire for a better relationship.
True. Having David around has really helped me find the courage to face some of these issues, too.
David seems to be a great support for you. Has his presence also influenced how you see your relationship with Lily?
Definitely. Watching how supportive he is and how we handle things together gives me hope that Lily and I can do the same.
It's beautiful to hear that. With empathy and patience, you can build a stronger connection with her.
I really hope so. It's comforting to know we're on better terms heading into my wedding planning.
Absolutely, it sounds like a positive step forward. How are you feeling about the wedding planning amidst everything?
Excited but also a bit overwhelmed. There’s so much to do, but having my sister there now feels reassuring.
It's a lot, but try to take it one step at a time. With loved ones by your side, especially Lily and David, it can also be a joyful experience.
Thanks, I needed to hear that. Focusing on the positive aspects really makes a difference.
I'm glad I could help. You’re doing great, Linda. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Hey, I just got back from the doctor.
Hi Linda. How did it go? Are you okay?
The doctor said my stress levels are through the roof. It was a bit of a wake-up call, honestly.
That sounds really concerning. I'm glad you went to see a doctor. What did they suggest?
They told me I need to find ways to manage my stress better. But with everything going on, it just feels overwhelming.
I can only imagine how much you're juggling right now. It makes sense that it's a lot to handle. Have you thought about any specific steps you might take?
I've been thinking about trying meditation, and maybe pick up some light exercise routines. But it's hard with the wedding planning and work stuff.
Those sound like great ideas. It's tough, but it might help you find some peace amidst the chaos. How's the wedding planning going, by the way?
It's exciting but also stressful. There's so much to organize and David and I are still figuring out some of the details.
It's understandable to feel that way. It's a big step, but also a joyous one. How have you and David been handling the pressure together?
David's been really supportive, especially after these health issues came up. He's been reminding me it's okay to slow down and take care of myself.
That's wonderful to hear. Having someone like David must be comforting. Have you thought about leaning on any of your other support systems?
I've reconnected with my sister Lily. She's been really understanding about everything that's happened in the past. We even laughed about our old arguments recently.
That's so heartening to hear, Linda. Family can be a great source of strength. How's it been with Buddy, your puppy?
Buddy is a little ball of energy. He makes me smile every day, which is helping a lot.
That's so lovely. Dogs can bring so much joy and relieve stress. It's good to hear you have a little bit of joy and laughter with him.
Yeah, it feels nice to have that balance, even just for moments. I'm just worried I won't keep up with everything and it'll affect my health again.
It's completely normal to feel that worry, Linda. It's tough, but take each day as it comes. Remember to prioritize your health, and lean on your support systems.
Thank you. I really appreciate these talks. It's like a breath of fresh air during all this chaos.
I'm always here to listen, Linda. You're doing an amazing job handling everything. Just take it one step at a time and remember you're not alone in this.
Hey, thanks for being here. I just need to talk a bit.
Of course, Linda. What's on your mind?
I've been trying to keep up with everything, but it's just a lot. Work, wedding plans, and now I've added meditation into the mix to help with stress.
It sounds like you have a lot on your plate. How is the meditation going so far?
It's been interesting. Some days it helps, and other days it's hard to focus. I keep thinking about the next thing I need to do.
That's understandable. It's hard to quiet the mind when so much is happening. Have you noticed any particular moments when stress hits the hardest?
Usually when I'm at home trying to relax, ironically. David is supportive, but I feel guilty about how much I'm depending on him.
Leaning on someone you love isn't a bad thing, Linda. Have you talked to David about how you're feeling?
Not in depth. I think I'm scared he'll think I'm not ready for the commitment if I show too much of my stress.
It's important to let him in on your struggles. He might surprise you with how understanding he is. Plus, it might ease some of your stress sharing it with him.
You're right. I suppose I've always been the type to handle things on my own, even when I was arguing with Lily. But, it's exhausting.
You've come a long way since then, reestablishing your bond with Lily and even adopting Buddy for emotional support. It's okay to embrace new support systems.
Buddy has been a joy, definitely helps lift my spirits on rough days. I forgot how much a pet can change the atmosphere.
Pets have a special way of comforting us. It's like they know when we need a little extra love. How's Buddy adjusting?
He's a bundle of energy and keeps me distracted in a good way. Sometimes, I wish I could have his carefree attitude.
Sounds like Buddy is a wonderful addition. And taking things one moment at a time, like he does, might help. How has your health been since the doctor's visit?
The meditation is helping, slowly. My doctor suggested regular breaks from wedding planning and work emails to keep things in balance.
That sounds like solid advice. Creating boundaries can be really beneficial. Would David be able to help with some of the planning?
I think he would. I've been hesitant to delegate, but maybe it's time to ease my load a bit.
Letting go of some of the responsibilities can relieve a lot of pressure. You're already doing so much just by working on your mental health.
Thank you. I guess I needed a reminder that it's okay to ask for help and not do everything alone.
Exactly. You're doing your best and that's all anyone can ask. Remember, you're not alone in this.
Thanks for talking this through with me. I feel a little lighter knowing I have support.
Anytime, Linda. Just keep breathing and reaching out whenever you need someone to listen.
Hey Linda, how have you been holding up lately?
Not too great, to be honest. Things are really tense between David and me right now.
I’m sorry to hear that. Is it about the wedding plans?
Yeah, we had our first big argument about it. It feels overwhelming.
Conflicts about wedding planning can be quite stressful. What specifically was the disagreement about?
David and I have different visions for the wedding, and it's hard to find a middle ground.
That sounds really challenging. Have you been able to talk it out since the argument?
We tried talking about it, but it's like we're speaking different languages on this topic.
It's tough to be on different pages with someone you care about. How are you feeling about the whole situation?
Honestly, I'm feeling anxious and it's triggering some of my previous stress issues.
Given your past experiences with stress, that must be really hard to navigate. Have you been keeping up with meditation or any other techniques to manage your anxiety?
I've been trying to meditate when I can, but it's difficult with everything else going on.
It's understandable that it might be difficult to focus right now. Maybe a small step could help, like setting aside just a few minutes each day?
That's a good idea, maybe I can try short sessions in the morning.
That sounds like a positive step. How's your relationship with your sister Lily going? I remember you two had reconnected recently.
It's been better. Lily's been supportive, which is nice, especially with everything going on right now.
It's great that you have her support. Maybe she could be someone to talk to about the wedding planning stresses too?
Yeah, I think it might help. She did offer to help once before all this started.
It might provide some relief to have a trusted family member involved. How about Buddy? How's your new puppy doing in all of this?
Buddy's been a little ball of sunshine. Having him around has been comforting.
Sometimes our pets give us just what we need, without even knowing it.
Definitely. It's nice to focus on his happiness even when things feel chaotic.
That’s wonderful. Remember, you’re not alone in this—between Buddy, Lily, and me, you have a great support system.
Thank you. It really helps knowing I can talk to you and lean on others.
Any time, Linda. I’m here whenever you need to talk or figure things out. Take it one step at a time.

current_prefix.text: Hi Amanda, it's good to see you online. How have you been doing lately?
Hey! I've been feeling a bit off after attending my aunt's memorial service last week.
I'm sorry to hear that. It must have been an emotional experience for you.
Yeah, it really was. Not only because we were saying goodbye, but also because I got to see so many relatives I hadn't seen in years.
That sounds like it brought up a lot of feelings. How did that affect you?
It was bittersweet. On one hand, it was wonderful to reconnect, but on the other hand, it made me realize how distant I've become from them.
It sounds like you're processing a mix of emotions—grief and perhaps some regret?
Exactly. I feel guilty for not staying in touch more. It was strange talking about memories with people I used to be so close to.
That's understandable. Guilt can be hard to shake off, but reconnecting at the memorial could be a new beginning.
I hope so. I exchanged numbers with a few of them and promised to keep in touch.
That's a great step forward. How does it feel to have taken that initiative?
A little reassuring, honestly. But there's still this nagging feeling of having missed out on so much with them.
It's natural to feel that way, but it's important to give yourself grace. Every relationship has its own timeline.
You're right. I guess I should focus on making the most of the present.

turns.text: hi there
Hello! How are you doing?
I'm not doing so good at the moment. I'm feeling very stressed and burned out from work
That sounds very frustrating. Is this a recent development at your job?
It's been building up for a while now, but it's really starting to get a but overwhelming
I can understand how that can have an effect on your mental well-being. Have you spoken to your supervisor about your frustrations at work?
I have, but sometimes I feel like she doesn't really listen and she sort of talks over me a lot
It sounds like you don't feel listened to.
That's right... I guess that is quite a lot of the problem.
I don't mind so much the work, I know it is busy for everyone right now, it's a combination of the workload plus not being listened to
I had a similar issue at my last job. My supervisor constantly spoke over me in meetings, and it would drive me crazy. I never could get a word in edge-wise.
Yeah, that sounds a lot like what I am experiencing
Are you considering switching jobs?
It's been in the back of my mind, but it's a hard time just now with everything else going on
Absolutely. It's a rough time job searching under the best of circumstances.
It is.
Have you tried reaching out to anyone in your network to look for a new position? It helped me when I was previously job searching.
I haven't, but it might be worth getting in touch with some people
Absolutely. I also spoke with a therapist before and it helped me a lot.
Have you considered reaching out to a professional to talk to?
I did consider that, but aren't they expensive?
They can be, but many local governments and municipalities have therapists that work on a sliding scale if the financial aspect of therapy is a concern.
Therapy can definitely be a large expense though.
It might be worth it in the long run though I guess, if it helps how I am feeling
If it helps to reframe the expense, you can try to think of it as an investment in your mental health.

I have not told her yet. I do not want to get her into trouble and I want to have a good relationship with her.

Can you discuss it with her in a respectful way to get her to understand that you're not trying to undermine her but that this is how you work most efficiently? And maybe mention that you don't want to involve the boss?
That's something I could try. I really care about my coworker and it makes me so angry that she treats me this way.

I think sometimes it's easy to jump to anger when you feel hurt. It might be worth telling her how you feel and also maybe ask why she thinks you should be doing things her way. Maybe there's a give and take in this situation. Some of her methods could be beneficial.
Do you have any advice on how to start my conversation with her? I have found some of her ideas to be beneficial. I just would like my ideas expressed as well. I feel we can learn from each other.

Tell her the things that you like about her method and maybe suggest some of your methods to her as well. Maybe she'll find them to be more efficient. Make it a partnership rather than a fight for whose method is better.
She could feel threatened by you so it's worth digging into those feelings with her and proving to her that you're working toward the same goal.

That's a great idea. It is possible. I am the new kid on the block. I will try by being non confrontational. Any specific ideas to how  I can do that? She gets offended easily. I want her to know I am helping.

I'd suggest how much she's helped you since you are in fact the new kid on the block.  And tell her that you want to work with her to have the most efficient partnership possible and use each of your talents to the best of your ability. Yeah, it's just that I thought we were going to build a life together, and now it's like I have to start over in a way.
It definitely feels overwhelming having to rethink your future plans. Do you feel like talking to your relatives again has given you any support?
Actually, yes. Since I reconnected with my family at my aunt's memorial, they've been really supportive. It's nice to know they're there for me.
That's so important, having a support system to lean on. Have you spoken to any of your friends or coworkers about it?
I told a few friends, and they've been great. Work's been a distraction, and ever since my coworker and I made up, it's been a more positive environment.
It sounds like you're doing a great job surrounding yourself with positive energy and support. What about self-care? Are you finding time for yourself?
I'm trying to. I watched a favorite movie and went for a long walk yesterday to clear my head. It's the little things, I guess.
Definitely, those small acts of self-care can make such a big difference. What do you feel like you need most right now?
I think I just need time to process everything, to let myself feel and heal without rushing into anything new.
Taking the time you need is so important. Give yourself grace, and don't hesitate to reach out if you need someone to talk to.
Thank you, that means a lot. I'll definitely keep that in mind.

Yes, exactly. I just feel like no matter how hard I try, my efforts aren't valued.

I'm trying to stay focused on the projects and find satisfaction in my work itself, but it's tough.

It's good to have even a little bit of support. Have you considered any strategies to improve the situation with your supervisor?
I've thought about it, but honestly, I feel stuck. I want to have an open dialogue, but every time I try, it backfires.

I think just talking about it helps. Sometimes I feel so alone in this, and it's reassuring to have someone listen.
I'm here anytime you need to talk. You're definitely not alone, and what you're feeling is completely valid.
Thanks, that really means a lot. I think I've also been emotionally drained since my breakup last month.
Breakups are incredibly tough, especially on top of everything else. Have you been able to find some personal time to process everything?
I've been trying to, but between work stress and personal life, it's been challenging to find time for myself.
It's important to carve out some 'you' time whenever you can. Perhaps it might help to set small boundaries, even if just for a moment of calm.
That's a good idea, actually. Maybe a short walk during lunch or some time reading a book could work.
That sounds perfect. Even small steps like that can make a huge difference in how you feel.
I'll try to make it a habit. I need something positive to focus on.
That's the spirit. Remember, I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're doing the best you can, and that's more than enough.
Thank you so much. Having someone to talk to really helps keep me grounded.
You're very welcome. Anytime you need me, just reach out. You've got this, Amanda.
Hi, I really need to talk about something that's been weighing on me recently.
Of course, Amanda. I'm here for you. What's going on?
I received another negative performance review from my supervisor, and it's really getting to me.
I'm so sorry to hear that. How are you feeling about the review?
It's just so frustrating. I feel like no matter how hard I work, it's never enough.
That's really tough. It sounds like you're putting in so much effort and not getting the recognition you deserve.
Exactly. It's not just this review; it's been a pattern with my supervisor for a while now.
That's understandable. It must be incredibly discouraging to face that repeatedly.
Yes, and it's starting to affect my motivation. I feel so undervalued.
Feeling undervalued at work can be so draining. Do you have any support or allies in the workplace that you can talk to about this?
I've mended things with a coworker recently, which has helped a bit. But it's still so lonely dealing with this.
I'm glad to hear that you have someone you can at least partially lean on. Have you thought about addressing this with anyone higher up or in HR?
I have, but I'm worried it might make things worse with my supervisor if they find out.
That's a valid concern. It's important to weigh the potential outcomes. How are you handling the stress outside of work?
Honestly, not well. The stress is impacting my personal life too, especially after my recent breakup.
It sounds like you're dealing with a lot on your plate all at once. It must be hard to find peace right now.
It is. I'm trying to stay connected with family, but I still feel quite lost.
Reconnecting with family after the memorial service was a positive step. It’s okay to lean on them for support in times like these.
You're right. I need to reach out more, even though it's hard.
Taking that step can be tough, but you have the strength to do it. Remember, you don’t have to go through any of this alone.
Thanks for saying that. I really appreciate your support.
Anytime, Amanda. I'm here whenever you need someone to talk to. You're not alone in this.
Hey Amanda, how are you holding up lately? Anything on your mind?
Hey, I just found out that Bill, my ex, is dating someone new. I didn't think it would affect me so much.
Oh Amanda, I'm sorry. It must be really tough to hear that news. How are you feeling about it?
I feel a mix of emotions. On one hand, I know we broke up for good reasons, but on the other, it still hurts seeing him move on so quickly.
It's completely understandable to feel that way. Breakups have a way of stirring up unexpected feelings. Would talking about it more with me help?
Maybe. I'm starting to question if I'm the one who's taking too long to move on. It's like I'm stuck in this limbo.
You're not stuck, you're just processing everything at your own pace. Everyone's journey is different, and it's okay to take the time you need.
I guess. But seeing him happy with someone else makes me doubt myself, like, was I not enough, or did I make the right choice?
Those are hard questions to grapple with. Remember, breaking up was about differences in life goals, not your worth or abilities. You did it for your future.
True, we did have differing goals. I just wish I could turn off the emotional part and focus on that rationality.
Emotions can be really stubborn like that. It's okay to feel and express them, though. They're part of being human and make us whole.
Yeah, I suppose. It's just exhausting at times, especially with everything else going on... like work stress.
I remember you mentioned how undervalued you feel at work. That must amplify everything. How is that going?
Not great. My supervisor is still making things difficult, and I recently got a negative performance review. It's been crushing my confidence.
That sounds incredibly challenging. Dealing with work stress on top of personal issues seems overwhelming. Have you considered seeking any outside support?
I thought about it. Maybe seeing a therapist could help, but it's intimidating to take that step.
It's a big step, but it can also be really empowering. Having a space to speak openly and get professional guidance might ease that burden.
You're right. I need to prioritize myself more. It's been hard juggling everything alone.
I'm glad you're considering it. Remember, you're not alone in this. Feel free to reach out whenever you need to talk.
Thanks. It helps knowing there's someone I can lean on. I'll think more seriously about getting support.
That's a great step forward, Amanda. I'm really proud of you for facing all of this and seeking the path that's best for you.
Hello how are you?
I'm, okay, thanks, and you?  I'm feeling a bit down because I'm alone for the holidays.
Well that's no good, does your family live far away?
Yes, my family is scattered all over the country, like Seattle, Georgia, PA.  I'm sure I'm not the only one with no plans this weekend, though.
True but I can understand that, it is hard being alone at the holidays.
Did you have plans this weekend?
No.  My nearby friends all went away for the holidays.  I could probably just occupy my time with things I need or want to do in order to distract myself.
What kind of hobbies do you have?
I'm teaching myself the piano.  I'm also teaching myself  how to work a stenography machine for possible future employment as a stenographer.  I also like to read novels.
I have never understood how those work..I find it amazing someone can type out whole words or sentences with one word
Yeah, it's pretty cool.  For example, if I hit DRAT in one stroke, then "Did there come a time" will appear in English on my machine's  LCD screen.
Wow that is crazy, I don't understand how that works, is it preprogrammed or does it go by how the word sounds?

Each stenographer has their own "Personal Dictionary" which is a list of words in English along with how you in particular write out those words or phrases in steno.  This dictionary is present within the actual steno machine after you transfer it from your laptop to the machine via cable or wifi.  Thus your machine then knows how you write out words in particular and how to translate those words from steno to English - each stenographer writes a little differently.
OK that makes sense, so you basically program it as the user. I take it your stenography machine becomes pretty close to you lol
Is this your first holiday alone?

Yes, exactly!  And it's very important to back up your personal dictionary to the cloud or a seperate drive so that you don't lose it in a hard-drive crash.  A lot of work goes into creating that dictionary!  No, it's happened before, being along for the holidays; but you've helped to cheer me up, so thanks!
No problem, I hope I have made your day a little better!
You have, thanks!  Did you do anything special?
Have a good rest of this year and don't forget to make your New Year's resolution!
I will do that - you too.  Thanks, again...
Not really, stayed home lol... Have a good one!
You too... bye now...
Good day!
What else can I help you with today?
